samples.question: This image shows a stretch of piano keyboard drawn on white paper. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks near the corners are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. The dark upright rectangles standing on the keyboard are the black keys; the pale keyboard body and its thin grey dividing lines are not black keys. The black keys are painted in groups. Two neighbouring black keys belong to the same group when the strip of pale keyboard between them is narrow; a gap more than twice as wide as the narrowest gap in this image separates one group from the next group. The number of groups, the number of black keys in each group, the width and height of the black keys, the width of the pale keys, the ink colour and the position of the keyboard on the page all change from image to image, and the keyboard drawn here need not follow the two-and-three grouping of a real piano. Read only what is painted in this image and do not answer from what a piano keyboard normally looks like. The leftmost group is the group of black keys nearest the left edge of the page. How many black keys are in the leftmost group? Answer with exactly one of the integers 1, 2, 3, or 4.
